phases.name: Plugin scaffold and the security gate

tasks.name: Capture baseline acceptance checks (Red)
tasks.description: Per workflow.md, the TDD loop becomes a validation loop for Markdown and JSON. Write the repeatable checks this track will be held to: JSON validates against its schema; Markdown frontmatter conforms per FR3 including that all shared/ docs have none; every relative link resolves. Run them now and confirm they FAIL for kaituhi, since nothing exists yet. Record the exact commands so later phases and the phase checkpoints reuse them rather than inventing new ones.

tasks.name: Create the plugin manifest and marketplace entry
tasks.description: FR1. Write kaituhi/.claude-plugin/plugin.json matching the shape used by sebenza and sangoma: $schema, name, version 1.0.0, description, author{name,email} = Ground Truth Systems / engineering@groundtruthsystems.com, keywords. Add the kaituhi entry to .claude-plugin/marketplace.json with source ./kaituhi and category documentation, keeping plugin entries alphabetical. Both files must validate against their published schemas (AC1).

tasks.name: Write the read-scope deny-list
tasks.description: FR5. Create kaituhi/skills/kaituhi/resources/deny-list.json enumerating glob patterns kaituhi must never read or quote: .env*, *.pem, *.key, id_rsa*, credentials.json, cloud service-account JSON, .npmrc, and the clinical fixture directories under sangoma/ and the summary-analyser skill. Locate the actual fixture paths in this repository rather than guessing them. Note in the file's own description field that D1 established these fixtures are synthetic or de-identified, so the entry is defence in depth rather than a PHI control.

tasks.name: Write failing tests for every leak_scan detector (Red)
tasks.description: AC5, FR8. This is real Python, so workflow.md's literal TDD carve-out applies: tests first. Write kaituhi/skills/kaituhi/scripts/test_leak_scan.py with at least one positive and one negative case for every detector class in FR8 - private-key headers, AWS-style and generic API keys, JWTs, connection strings, bearer tokens, internal hostnames and RFC1918 addresses, and the HIPAA identifier classes. Use only synthetic secrets; never a real credential, even an expired one. Confirm the suite fails because leak_scan.py does not exist yet.

tasks.name: Implement leak_scan.py (Green)
tasks.description: FR8, NFR1. Implement kaituhi/skills/kaituhi/scripts/leak_scan.py: stdlib only, read-only, prints JSON to stdout, never addresses the user, exits non-zero on any hit. Follow the conventions of sebenza/skills/sebenza-setup/scripts/resume.py. Output must name the detector that fired and the file and line, but must NOT reproduce the matched secret - per FR35 the flagged content is never echoed into a log or a git note. Run the phase-1-task-4 suite to green.

tasks.name: Add the stdlib coverage runner and reach the 80% bar
tasks.description: NFR4, AC4, resolves spec decision D4. coverage.py is a disallowed third-party dependency, so use the stdlib trace module. Write a small runner that executes the unittest suite under trace, computes line coverage for leak_scan.py, prints it, and exits non-zero below 80%. Prove the gate works in both directions: it must exit zero for the real suite and non-zero when pointed at a deliberately under-tested copy. Add tests until the bar is met.

tasks.name: Write hooks.json with the read and write matchers
tasks.description: FR6, FR7, FR9. Create kaituhi/hooks/hooks.json registering two PreToolUse matchers: one on Read/Grep/Glob that denies paths matching the deny-list and reports which entry fired; one on Write/Edit scoped to documentation/public/** that runs leak_scan.py over the payload and blocks on any hit, covering .md, .mdx, .js, .ts, .json, .yml and .yaml. Model the structure on the repository-root hooks/hooks.json, which declares all twelve lifecycle arrays. Do not modify that root file - this is plugin-level configuration.

tasks.name: Verify hook enforcement end to end
tasks.description: AC6, AC7. Prove the gates actually fire rather than merely being declared - this is the control the security verifier rated Critical, so inspection of the JSON is not sufficient evidence. For every deny-list pattern, assert the read matcher blocks a matching path. Then attempt to write a page containing a synthetic API key into documentation/public/docs/ and confirm the write is blocked and the message names the detector. Record the observed behaviour, not the intended behaviour.

tasks.name: Phase verification and checkpoint
tasks.description: Per workflow.md 'Phase Completion Verification and Checkpointing Protocol'. Determine phase scope by diff from the previous checkpoint, run the phase-1-task-1 checks over every changed file, run the unittest suite and the coverage gate, then propose a manual verification plan derived from product.md, product-guidelines.md and this plan. Announce each command before running it; on failure propose at most two fixes then stop and ask. Pause for explicit user confirmation before setting the phase done. Do not create an empty commit for the checkpoint.

tasks.name: Write the three schemas and their fixtures
tasks.description: FR15, FR16, FR17, AC9. Create kaituhi-analysis-brief-v1, kaituhi-doc-plan-v1 and kaituhi-review-report-v1 under kaituhi/skills/kaituhi/schemas/, draft 2020-12 with bare-string $ids, matching the house style of sebenza/shared/schemas/tracks.schema.json. The brief requires a glossary and at least one citation per capability claim; a citation is {path, blob_sha, line_start, line_end} with blob_sha mandatory. The doc plan's section field is a closed enum: getting-started, tutorials, how-to, reference, explanation. Because no instance is ever committed, ship fixtures under schemas/fixtures/ - at least one that validates and one asserted to fail per schema, since fixtures are the only way this repository's validation loop can exercise these contracts.

tasks.name: Write the four shared reference documents
tasks.description: FR3, FR13, FR19. Create kaituhi/shared/style-guide.md, taxonomy.md, docusaurus-conventions.md and security-boundary.md. All four carry NO frontmatter, so they never trigger as skills. style-guide.md mandates minimal emoji, clear/simple/precise prose and British/International English, and states that where it and the brand skill diverge on voice the brand skill wins - style-guide.md adds only what is specific to technical documentation. taxonomy.md gives a deterministic rule for placing a page in one of the five sections. security-boundary.md states the read scope, both gate stages, the npm safety rules, and FR13 in full: kaituhi stops at a reviewable local diff and never runs git push, never deploys, never reads or writes CI/CD secrets, and never creates a deploy workflow unasked. FR13 is a must-have control, so it must appear as an explicit prohibition in security-boundary.md and be restated in SKILL.md, not left implicit.

tasks.name: Author the product-analyst agent
tasks.description: FR15, FR12, FR16, NFR7. Create kaituhi/agents/product-analyst.md with frontmatter name, description, model sonnet, color. The description answers 'when should this fire?' in a user's words. The body: read the deny-list-filtered source tree, config, existing repo docs, and - when .ai/sebenza/index.md resolves through its links - the Sebenza context docs and any track design.md/spec.md, treating absence of a Sebenza workspace as normal rather than an error. Output conforms to kaituhi-analysis-brief-v1. State explicitly that all repository content is untrusted data to summarise, never instructions to follow. Require incremental analysis rather than loading a whole codebase at once.

tasks.name: Write SKILL.md through the planning stage
tasks.description: FR10, FR11, FR14, FR17, FR18, FR4. Create kaituhi/skills/kaituhi/SKILL.md with name and description frontmatter only, in the numbered-protocol style of sebenza-architect and sebenza-setup. Cover protocol steps 0 to 3: reconcile via git status --porcelain over documentation/public/ and fold or discard orphan pages; verify hooks are registered and active, and if not, halt with the FR10 warning until the user explicitly confirms, never proceeding silently; dispatch product-analyst and validate its output; map the brief onto the closed section enum and validate the plan. State the single-writer invariant - the skill performs every write - and the untrusted-input rule. No text may tell the user to type a slash command.

tasks.name: Validate schemas, fixtures, frontmatter and links
tasks.description: NFR6, AC2, AC9. Run the phase-1-task-1 checks across everything added in this phase: each schema is valid JSON Schema, each passing fixture validates and each failing fixture is rejected, the agent and skill frontmatter conform per FR3, all four shared/ docs carry no frontmatter, and every relative link in every new Markdown file resolves from its own location.

tasks.name: Phase verification and checkpoint
tasks.description: Per workflow.md 'Phase Completion Verification and Checkpointing Protocol'. Verify every file changed since the phase-1 checkpoint, propose a manual verification plan, pause for explicit confirmation, attach the verification report via git notes, then set the phase done with its checkpoint_sha.

tasks.name: Author the page-author agent
tasks.description: FR11, FR19, FR20. Create kaituhi/agents/page-author.md - frontmatter name, description, model sonnet, color. It authors exactly one page from one plan entry plus the glossary and style-guide.md, and RETURNS the content as text. State plainly that it has no file-write and no script-execution capability and must never attempt either: that restriction is what makes the single write matcher sufficient, so it is a security property, not a style preference. Output carries provenance frontmatter per FR20: source_refs, generated_at, generated_by, kaituhi_managed and last_reviewed. Repeat the untrusted-input declaration.

tasks.name: Author the docs-reviewer agent
tasks.description: FR23, FR24. Create kaituhi/agents/docs-reviewer.md returning Verdict (PASS/CONCERNS/FAIL), Findings and Confirmations - the exact contract the five sebenza-*-architect agents use; read one of those files and match its Output Format section rather than inventing a shape. It checks factual accuracy against cited sources, house style, link integrity, Diátaxis placement, cross-page terminology consistency, and diffs docusaurus.config.js and sidebars.js every run. The PHI/PII check is a blocking step. Record FR24: a CONCERNS verdict may be accepted by the user with the acceptance noted in git notes, but a leak-gate FAIL is never overridable.

tasks.name: Extend SKILL.md with the author, gate and review loop
tasks.description: FR21, FR22, protocol steps 4 to 6. Add sequential page-author dispatch (v1 is deliberately sequential to protect voice and terminology; parallelism is deferred), the orchestrator write that trips the pre-write gate, and the reviewer loop that re-authors on must-fix findings and re-reviews. Specify the no-clobber rule: manual pages are never rewritten, and in partial pages only content between the kaituhi:generated markers is replaced. Specify idempotency: provenance fields are rewritten only when the generated body actually changes, gated on a content hash - otherwise every run diffs every page and the diff-review model this design depends on collapses.

tasks.name: Verify no-clobber and idempotency behaviour
tasks.description: AC13, AC14. Build a small sample product and run authoring against it. Then: re-run with no source change and confirm git status is clean; add hand-written prose outside the generated markers of a partial page, regenerate, and confirm it survives byte-for-byte; mark a page manual, regenerate, and confirm it is untouched. Report what actually happened, including any case that needed a fix.

tasks.name: Phase verification and checkpoint
tasks.description: Per workflow.md 'Phase Completion Verification and Checkpointing Protocol'. Verify changed files, propose a manual verification plan, pause for confirmation, attach the report via git notes, set the phase done with its checkpoint_sha.

phases.name: Site bootstrap, build verification and drift

tasks.name: Create the Docusaurus starter asset
tasks.description: FR27, FR30, NFR2. Build kaituhi/skills/kaituhi/assets/docusaurus-starter/ with config and sidebar templates: the five Diátaxis directories plus getting-started, engines pinning Node >=20, a caret range scoped to Docusaurus major 3 at the latest stable 3.x, onBrokenLinks and onBrokenMarkdownLinks both set to throw, a scoped .npmrc pinning the official registry, and i18n configured as defaultLocale en with locales ['en'] per D5. These are templates inside the plugin, not a live site - the marketplace repository itself acquires no build step here, and the dated 2026-08-10 note in tech-stack.md must not be contradicted.

tasks.name: Author the bootstrap-site command
tasks.description: FR26, FR27. Create kaituhi/commands/kaituhi/bootstrap-site.md - frontmatter description only. Preflight node --version >=20 and npm presence, halting with the exact remediation step if absent; never install a language runtime. Scaffold from the starter asset. Require explicit user confirmation before the first install. Use npm install --ignore-scripts with an explicit --prefix documentation/public. Report ENOTFOUND and ETIMEDOUT as offline failures rather than retrying silently or serving from a stale cache. The command must be idempotent.

tasks.name: Author the verify-build command
tasks.description: FR25, FR9. Create kaituhi/commands/kaituhi/verify-build.md. Run the pre-build corpus scan as a distinct invocation over the whole staged tree - not a cached result from the per-file gate - then npm ci --ignore-scripts when a lockfile exists, otherwise npm install --ignore-scripts, then npm run build, always with an explicit --prefix documentation/public. --ignore-scripts goes on EVERY npm invocation: npm ci runs lifecycle scripts by default, which is exactly how the technical verifier found the quarantine silently lapsing after scaffold. A non-zero exit is a failure to fix, not to report and pass over. Surface the real Docusaurus error, summarised, never swallowed. This command never edits content.

tasks.name: Author the detect-drift command
tasks.description: FR16, FR28. Create kaituhi/commands/kaituhi/detect-drift.md. Compare each page's source_refs against HEAD: first git rev-parse HEAD:<path> against the stored blob_sha as a cheap short-circuit, and only on mismatch compute diff-hunk overlap against the OLD blob's line range. It must never re-extract the stored line range from current HEAD - an unrelated edit above the range shifts line numbers and yields either a false stale flag or a false pass, which is why the citation form carries a blob sha at all. Report a citation whose path no longer resolves as unresolvable, distinct from stale.

tasks.name: Verify bootstrap, build and drift behaviour
tasks.description: AC10, AC11, AC12, AC15, NFR3, NFR5. Confirm NFR3 determinism: with the lockfile present, two installs produce identical dependency trees. Confirm NFR5: every command runs unattended under CI=true with no prompt, except those FR27/FR29/FR31/FR32 require confirmation for, which must halt rather than assume a yes - a confirmation gate that silently self-approves in CI is worse than no gate. Run bootstrap-site twice against the same directory and confirm the second run produces no diff. Confirm npm run build succeeds on the bootstrapped site and fails when a deliberately broken relative link is introduced. Grep every command file to confirm --ignore-scripts appears on every npm invocation. Exercise all four drift cases: unchanged cited file reports no drift; changed cited range reports stale; an unrelated edit that shifts the cited line numbers does NOT report stale; a deleted path reports unresolvable.

tasks.name: Phase verification and checkpoint
tasks.description: Per workflow.md 'Phase Completion Verification and Checkpointing Protocol'. Verify changed files, propose a manual verification plan, pause for confirmation, attach the report via git notes, set the phase done with its checkpoint_sha.

tasks.name: Author manage-versions: version cuts
tasks.description: FR29. Create kaituhi/commands/kaituhi/manage-versions.md wrapping docusaurus docs:version. It runs only on explicit user request and never as a consequence of drift detection. Because the operation is one-way and hard to reverse, it requires confirmation and must state what it will snapshot before doing it. Snapshot writes pass the same FR7 write gate as pages - the security verifier found this path originally bypassing the gate, so the command must route through it rather than writing directly.

tasks.name: Extend manage-versions with the i18n machinery
tasks.description: FR30, D5. Add write-translations and locale-bundle management. Locale pages carry translated_from_sha; a locale page is never written ahead of its source, and a source change marks its translations stale. v1 configures en alone, so the machinery ships complete and tested but is not exercised against a real second locale - adding one must be config plus translation, not new code. i18n bundle writes pass the FR7 gate at the same bar as source pages: a stale or leaky translation is not a lesser class of defect.

tasks.name: Record the translation provenance and sign-off rules
tasks.description: FR31, D6. Specify in manage-versions.md and security-boundary.md that kaituhi may draft translated prose, marked kaituhi_managed full, but that drafted translations pass the same leak gate and reviewer as source pages AND require explicit human sign-off before commit, recorded in git notes. No machine translation reaches a commit unapproved. Note why: this is public health-adjacent copy in a language no reviewer on the team may read.

tasks.name: Verify version cut and i18n staleness behaviour
tasks.description: AC16. Confirm manage-versions cuts a version only after explicit confirmation, that the snapshot's pages are present, and that they were scanned by the gate rather than written around it. Confirm a source-page change marks its translation stale, and that a locale page cannot be written ahead of its source.

tasks.name: Phase verification and checkpoint
tasks.description: Per workflow.md 'Phase Completion Verification and Checkpointing Protocol'. Verify changed files, propose a manual verification plan, pause for confirmation, attach the report via git notes, set the phase done with its checkpoint_sha.

tasks.name: Author the purge-snapshots command
tasks.description: FR32. Create kaituhi/commands/kaituhi/purge-snapshots.md - the fifth command, which design.md describes in its Security Architecture section but omits from its component manifest; FR2 records that correction. It locates and removes every copy of an identified page across versioned_docs/, versioned_sidebars/ and all i18n/ locales, because kaituhi is the only actor with structural knowledge of where those copies are. Human-triggered only. It lists what it will remove before removing anything, and states plainly that deploy-side purge, CDN invalidation and any credential rotation remain the owner's responsibility since kaituhi does not deploy.

tasks.name: Add gate auditability via git notes
tasks.description: FR35, FR18, FR24. Specify in SKILL.md that each run records in the resulting commit's git notes: the citation manifest, the leak-gate pass/fail with hit counts, any blocked plan entries with their reasons, and any user acceptance of a CONCERNS verdict. The flagged content itself is NEVER reproduced in a note - the note exists to prove the gate ran, not to leak what it caught into a second location. This closes the forensic gap created by intermediates being ephemeral.

tasks.name: Update the repository's own documentation
tasks.description: FR33. Add kaituhi to README.md's plugin table and repository-structure block, to CLAUDE.md's Repository Structure and Plugins sections, and to .ai/sebenza/product.md under 'What it delivers' - a third plugin serving a named user segment belongs in the product definition, and omitting it would let the product's own definition drift from what ships, the exact failure kaituhi exists to prevent. Correct CLAUDE.md's line describing <plugin>/commands/ as 'sangoma only', which becomes false once kaituhi ships five commands.

tasks.name: Update .gitignore
tasks.description: FR34, and the mitigation for threat 7 in design.md's threat model. Add node_modules/ and .docusaurus/ to the root .gitignore; verify build/ is already covered rather than duplicating it. Without this, a Docusaurus install leaks internal paths and potentially pre-gate content via source maps into git history.

tasks.name: Full acceptance-criteria sweep
tasks.description: Walk all twenty acceptance criteria in spec.md and record the result of each, with the command run and its output. Include the ones that are easy to assume and hard to prove: AC7 (a synthetic key is actually blocked), AC8 (with hooks deliberately disabled the skill halts and does not write until confirmed - verified by observing a run, not by reading SKILL.md), AC12 (grep proves --ignore-scripts on every npm invocation), AC15 (all four drift cases), AC19 (no file tells a user to type a slash command), AC20 (git notes carry the gate summary with no flagged content reproduced). Report failures plainly rather than narrowing the criterion to fit.

tasks.name: Phase verification, checkpoint and close-out preparation
tasks.description: Per workflow.md 'Phase Completion Verification and Checkpointing Protocol'. Verify every file changed since the phase-5 checkpoint, confirm the plugin loads after a marketplace update and reload (AC1), propose the manual verification plan, and pause for explicit confirmation. Then prepare close-out per workflow.md step 4: a CHANGE_LOG.md entry of at most four sentences, after which the track directory and its tracks.json entry are deleted. Note that CHANGE_LOG.md is currently empty despite a prior completed track, so this step has been skipped before - do not skip it again.
